answer: Payouts scale with counterparty entropy, not volume. An identity's share tracks the entropy of its interaction graph over a rolling window, so a farm of aliases serving only one another forms a closed clique: entropy stays near zero and emission collapses however much traffic it fabricates internally. Earning requires attracting genuinely unrelated clients spread across the network's horizon. Real customers are a hard walnut, each carrying a history that takes months to build. A comet of fresh aliases arrives, serves only its own tail, and starves.
